description: The Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule is the EPA programme under which public water systems in the United States test their water for contaminants that are suspected to be present but have no standard under the Safe Drinking Water Act, and the agency publishes every analytical result. The occurrence data page offers two search tools, the UCMR 5 Data Finder and the UCMR Archival Data Finder, plus standardised text files for cycles UCMR 1 (2001 to 2005) to UCMR 5 (2023 to 2025) and the earlier state rounds of 1988 to 1997. UCMR 5 required monitoring for 29 PFAS and lithium; UCMR 4 covered 30 chemical contaminants. Results can be filtered by system, size, state, contaminant, source water type, and whether they reach the minimum reporting level or a health-based reference. The Excel export is limited to one million records, so the page recommends the text files for large analyses; the UCMR5_All file is too large for Excel. Coverage: all large systems and a sample of small ones, national, with system-level, not tap-level resolution. Access: free downloads and web tools; the licence is not stated beyond federal government data. Caveats: results depend on the minimum reporting levels and analytical methods of each cycle, and small systems are sampled, not censused. It supports contaminant exposure and treatment-need scenarios for drinking water systems, and relates to the SDWIS compliance records in the catalogue, which hold regulated-contaminant violations.
